div.div:
Reading the gate line
wait — the wave is Ready when the objects it applies are Ready. healthChecks / healthCheckExprs — wait is deliberately absent: the objects worth gating on are StatefulSets and GrafanaManifests an operator creates later, so they are never in the wave's own applied set and wait would pass instantly. Listing them is the only thing that holds the next wave back (RFC-0028 / ADR-065). The two are mutually exclusive and wait wins, so a wave setting both gates only on what it applies.

div.style: display: flex; align-items: unsafe flex-start; justify-content: unsafe flex-start; width: 1228px; height: 1px; padding-top: 1135px; margin-left: 12px;

display: inline-block; font-size: 11px; font-family: Helvetica; color: light-dark(#475569, #9ba7b8); line-height: 1.2; pointer-events: all; white-space: normal; word-wrap: normal;

div.div:
Sources and scope
Every wave reads infrastructure-oci (oci://homelab-registry:5000/flux-infra-sync, ref local) except apps-local, which reads apps-oci (flux-apps-sync), and the two dashboards-as-code waves, which read grafana-dashboards-as-code-oci (ghcr.io/duynhlab/grafana-dashboards-as-code, semver 0.7.0). apps-local also waits for databases-local, temporal-config-local and keda-local, which sit outside this diagram.
